short_caption: Filtered positive residual culinary corridors after a geographic distance baseline. Blue links highlight East/Southeast Asia; orange links show global discovery candidates.
expanded_caption: This map shows cuisine pairs whose observed ingredient similarity is higher than the distance-only model predicts. Blue links foreground the East/Southeast Asia focused case, while orange links show candidate residual corridors from the broader global screen. Line width represents residual strength. The figure introduces the core spatial idea: the project is not simply mapping similar cuisines, but mapping where similarity exceeds geographic expectation.
alt_text: World map with colored lines connecting cuisine anchor locations. Blue links cluster around East and Southeast Asia; orange links show other positive residual cuisine connections across the global discovery screen.
what_to_notice: Look for places where similarity appears as a line after distance has already been modeled. The lines are candidates for focused interpretation, not historical routes.
source_note: Run 4 revised figure from filtered Run 2 v2 residual corridor outputs and cuisine coordinate crosswalk.
limitation_note: Discovery layer only; it does not prove global culinary causality or representative coverage.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; enable expand image if possible
short_caption: Cuisine similarity is plotted against log geographic distance. Points above the fitted trend become positive residual corridors.
expanded_caption: The scatterplot shows how the project turns ingredient similarity into spatial analysis. The fitted line is the distance baseline: the model’s estimate of how similar two cuisines should be given their geographic separation. Points above that line have positive residuals, meaning observed similarity is higher than distance alone predicts. Those residuals are the project’s central spatial object.
alt_text: Scatter plot of cuisine-pair similarity against log geographic distance with a downward fitted trend line. Points above the line are interpreted as positive residual cuisine pairs.
what_to_notice: The key move is the comparison between observed similarity and distance-predicted similarity. The interesting points are above the baseline.
source_note: Run 4 revised figure from filtered cuisine similarity and pairwise distance model outputs.
limitation_note: The distance model establishes spatial expectation and residuals; it is not a causal model.

storymap_section: Finding 3 / East and Southeast Asia primary case
recommended_display_size: Full-width image or sidecar media panel
short_caption: East/Southeast Asia focused case using filtered positive residual cuisine links. Thicker blue links indicate stronger positive residual similarity.
expanded_caption: This focused map narrows the global discovery screen to the strongest regional case. It highlights positive residual links among Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, and Filipino cuisine anchors. Because the subset is geographically coherent and contains enough cuisines for pairwise comparison, it supports the strongest non-causal spatial interpretation in the project.
alt_text: Regional map of East and Southeast Asia with cuisine anchor points connected by blue residual links, including Thai-Vietnamese, Chinese-Korean, Filipino-Thai, Filipino-Vietnamese, and Chinese-Filipino relationships.
what_to_notice: Notice how the strongest links sit within or across coherent East and Southeast Asian subregions rather than being scattered globally.
source_note: Run 4 revised focused-case figure from Run 2 v2 focus-case outputs and cuisine coordinates.
limitation_note: Focused inference case; still not proof of a specific historical mechanism.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; place immediately after primary case map
short_caption: East/Southeast Asia residual links over shaded relief and coastal context. The figure makes the focused corridor visually legible.
expanded_caption: This relief-context map places the strongest East/Southeast Asia residual links over terrain, coastlines, islands, peninsulas, and maritime space. It helps the viewer read Thai-Vietnamese as a compact mainland link, Chinese-Korean as a regional East Asian link, and Filipino links as island/maritime relationships. The map strengthens the spatial interpretation of the focused case without claiming that terrain or maritime movement caused the similarities.
alt_text: Shaded-relief map of East and Southeast Asia with cuisine residual links drawn over mainland, coastal, island, and maritime contexts. The Thai-Vietnamese, Chinese-Korean, and Filipino-related links are emphasized.
what_to_notice: The same residual links become easier to interpret when placed over relief, coasts, islands, and maritime space.
source_note: Run 5 figure using East/Southeast Asia residual/accessibility metrics, cuisine coordinates, and local Basemap ETOPO-style relief context.
limitation_note: Spatial context only; not a least-cost route model, terrain-causality model, or proof of migration/trade routes.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; emphasize as key Fisher contribution
short_caption: Residual bridge index by cuisine. The index aggregates positive residual links into mapped place-level bridge roles.
expanded_caption: The residual bridge index converts pairwise residual links into place-level spatial roles. It combines positive residual degree, top-residual participation, mean residual strength, long-distance residual score, and mean residual into a mapped index. This is the clearest spatial-necessity result: ingredient vectors alone can identify similar cuisines, but only GIS can show which mapped cuisine anchors repeatedly bridge residual similarities after distance is modeled.
alt_text: Map or chart showing cuisines as place-level nodes with bridge-index values, identifying which cuisine anchors participate in multiple unexpectedly strong residual links.
what_to_notice: Look for cuisines whose residual links are not isolated. A high bridge score means a cuisine participates repeatedly in unexpectedly strong spatial links.
source_note: Run 4 geospatial upgrade using filtered residual corridor outputs and coordinate anchors.
limitation_note: Bridge roles describe residual-network position; they do not identify historical pathways or causal mechanisms.

short_caption: Boundary/permeability diagnostic summarizing mean residual similarity by spatial grouping.
expanded_caption: This diagnostic figure compares residual similarity across spatial groupings such as same subregion, cross-subregion, East/Southeast Asia cross-subregion, Iberian/Atlantic interregional, and other cross-region links. It supports the idea that residual cuisine similarity has spatial structure, while also showing why the broad global result should remain a discovery screen rather than a causal explanation.
alt_text: Diagnostic chart comparing mean residual cuisine similarity across spatial groupings and secondary corridor classes.
what_to_notice: Use this figure as a caution layer. It shows structure, but also reminds the viewer that some long-distance groups require careful interpretation.
source_note: Run 4 revised figure from Run 2 v2 boundary/permeability summaries.
limitation_note: Diagnostic figure; not primary proof and not a causal mechanism.
